parsed.explanation: The quoted dichotomy does not follow from §3. That section excludes only two distinct positive values of g; it never excludes negative values, and earlier establishes merely g(x)>-x. Thus V could not yet be asserted to lie in {0,c}, so the later partition into S_0 and S_c is unsupported. The gap is repairable by observing that if g(u)=c<0, then (4) inductively gives f^n(u)=u+nc>0 for every n, contradicting u+nc≤0 for sufficiently large n. However, this argument is not written anywhere in the proof. Since all subsequent necessity arguments rely on V⊆{0,c}, the necessity proof is incomplete as written.
